title: docs(agents): re-point the Documentation Guardrails ghost `content/docs/guides/` row
body:
Fixes #11079

The Documentation Guardrails table carried a row for `content/docs/guides/`, a directory that does not exist. This re-points that row at the trees that do exist, keeping the `meta.json` rule it carried.

## Governed surface — draft only, human merge

`AGENTS.md` is on the governed-surface register (`docs/adr/**` · `.claude/**` · `skills/**` · `AGENTS.md` · `CLAUDE.md`). This PR **opens as draft and stays draft**: it must never be flipped ready, must not get auto-merge, and is **human merge only**.

## Evidence: re-point, not drop

The card allowed dropping the row *if* the rule it carries were already stated for the real trees elsewhere in the table. It is not — so the row is re-pointed.

**1. `content/docs/guides/` never existed. No tree "took over" it.**

There is no rename trail to follow, because there is nothing to follow from — across all 512 commits reachable in this repo, no path matching `*guides*` was ever added, renamed or deleted:

```
$ git log --all --oneline --follow -- 'content/docs/guides'      # (empty)
$ git log --all --oneline --diff-filter=D -- 'content/docs/guides/*'   # (empty)
$ git log --all --oneline --name-only --diff-filter=ADR -- '*guides*'  # (empty)
$ git rev-list --all --count
512
```

The row was a ghost from the start, not a stale pointer to relocated content. The issue's suggested targets (`getting-started/` / `capabilities/`) are therefore not "the tree that took over" — `getting-started/` was already its own row in this table, and `capabilities/` is simply one more hand-written tree among many.

**2. The `meta.json` rule is real, and this row was its ONLY statement in AGENTS.md.**

```
$ grep -n 'meta\.json' AGENTS.md
547:| `content/docs/guides/` | hand-written | ✅ Update `meta.json` when adding pages. |
```

One hit, on the ghost row. Dropping the row would have deleted the rule from the file outright.

**3. The rule applies to every hand-written tree, not to one special tree.**

All 13 hand-written trees have their own `meta.json`, and every one is an explicit ordered `pages` array with **no** rest-spread (`"..."`), so a page added but not listed does not appear in the nav:

```
$ grep -l '"\.\.\."' $(find content/docs -name meta.json)   # (empty — all explicit)
$ for d in ai api automation capabilities concepts data-modeling deployment \
           getting-started kernel permissions plugins protocol ui; do ...
ai: pages=9 mdx=9          api: pages=12 mdx=12       automation: pages=10 mdx=10
capabilities: pages=11 mdx=11   concepts: pages=6 mdx=6    data-modeling: pages=18 mdx=18
deployment: pages=12 mdx=12     getting-started: pages=11  kernel: pages=8
permissions: pages=21 mdx=21    plugins: pages=5 mdx=5     protocol: pages=7
ui: pages=17
```

(Trees whose `pages` count exceeds their top-level `.mdx` count reference subdirectories — `kernel/contracts/`, `protocol/objectql/` and friends.)

**4. Cross-checked against the gate-owned list.** `check:docs-audit-scope` maintains the generated `ALL_HANDWRITTEN` block in `.claude/workflows/docs-accuracy-audit.js` — 189 hand-written docs across 14 trees plus 3 root files. It contains no `guides` path. That list is regenerated from the tree, so it is the authoritative population; the prose row was the only thing claiming `guides/` exists.

Because the trees are enumerated and kept fresh by that gate, the replacement row deliberately **does not enumerate** them — an enumeration in prose is exactly the drift class this issue reports. It is defined by exclusion instead (`every tree except references/ and releases/ above`), which stays correct when a tree is added.

## The change

One row in, one row out:

```diff
-| `content/docs/guides/` | hand-written | ✅ Update `meta.json` when adding pages. |
+| `content/docs/<tree>/` — every tree except `references/` and `releases/` above | hand-written | ✅ Update that tree's own `meta.json` when adding a page: each is an explicit ordered `pages` array with no rest-spread, so a page you add but never list is absent from the nav. The rows below are named examples, not the whole set. |
```

The `concepts/` / `getting-started/` / `protocol/` rows below are untouched; the replacement row now says out loud that they are examples rather than the complete set, which was the second half of the original row's misleading effect.

## Ratchet

`AGENTS.md` is at its ceiling with zero headroom, so the change is line-neutral (1 insertion, 1 deletion, one file). `pnpm check:pm-skill-ratchet` verdict line:

```
✓ check-skill-line-ratchet: AGENTS.md is 961 lines (ceiling 961; headroom 0).
```

## Gates

Derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` on the actual change set (the script read the change set from the merge base itself; it reported `1 path(s)` — `AGENTS.md`). All 7 matched families run green, as a union at `d4c72da9`:

| `check:pm-governed-prose` | `✓ 2 instruction surface(s) name all 5 registered governed surfaces … and claim no others.` |
